generator_view.scenario: A buyer has a $100 ceiling for a gaming keyboard and is comparing a wired SK61 optical route, a wired Keychron K6 mechanical route, and paying more for an advertised 8000 Hz route. They require wired NKRO, prefer switch-replacement flexibility, and will pay a latency premium only when the frozen evidence establishes a product-specific benefit rather than a generic mechanism or owner impression.
generator_view.target: Audit the frozen product bodies, rollover and polling mechanisms, optical-switch claims, and community uncertainty, then choose one route without treating a theoretical poll period, seller wording, or owner opinion as a measured product-specific or perceptible aim benefit.

query: I have a total budget 100 dollars for a gaming keyboard. Wired NKRO required, and switch replacement flexibility priority. Compare the Keychron K6 wired NKRO value, SK61 optical NKRO value, and premium 8000Hz claim route. I do not pay for unverified 8000Hz claim. Audit each complete frozen product body for price, review display, key count, wired operation, NKRO mode, switch and hot-swap wording, any internal inconsistency, and whether polling or measured-latency fields are actually present. Explain what NKRO physically provides and why it does or does not establish faster single-key input or better aim. Reconcile optical sensing, contact debouncing, and the owner discussion, with community opinions are scoped. Define polling and USB HID reporting and calculate the poll periods for hypothetical 8000Hz and 1000Hz rates, but separate poll period from end to end latency. Also separate mechanism from human perceptibility; seller claims are not independent tests. Recommend one route under these priorities, state what the frozen sources cannot establish, and cite each factual claim to its sandbox source.
